newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -BT puts bought for dividend arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -BT puts bought for dividend arbitrage.

text.p: Traded options in British Telecommunications stood out for a dividend arbitrage deal in an otherwise subdued equity options market on Monday, dealers said.
Technical buying of in-the-money put options in BT was the main deal in UK stock options.
The deal was to buy 10,000 August 550 puts at 150p and 148-1/2p as well as sell 10,000 August 550 calls at 1-1/2p by a trader who also bought 10 million BT shares at about 418p-419p.
It comes ahead of a special dividend payment by BT owing to its proposed merger with MCI Communications of the U.S.

BT shares are due to go ex-dividend by 35p net on August 11 as a result of this proposed merger and once the shares have gone ex-dividend, the options buyer will be free to exercise his put options -- to sell five million BT shares at 550p -- and still collect the dividend.
The net cost of buying options plus shares is about 567p and the net credit from exercising the puts and collecting the dividend is 585p which locks in an overall profit of 18p.
And if the share price stays below 550 by August expiry, a further 1-1/2p profit can be from the short call position.
Dealers noted there have been a number of similar trades involving BT options which have been executed recently designed to lock in a profit.
By 1500 GMT, BT shares were up 7p to 421-1/2p.
